quarters.supplementaryReportName: Supplementary Financial Information trend table (as republished in Q2 2026 Supplementary Financial Information)

notes.roe: Reported ROE (annualized) per CIBC Supplementary Financial Information nine-quarter trend table.
notes.nim: Net interest margin on average interest-earning assets, as disclosed by CIBC.
notes.netIncomeMillions: Net income attributable to equity shareholders.
notes.source: All ratios/figures pulled from the nine-quarter 'Financial Highlights' and 'Balance sheet quality and liquidity measures' trend tables in CIBC's Q2 2026 Supplementary Financial Information package (which restates Q3/24 alongside Q2/26), cross-checked against the Q3 2024 news release for revenue/net income figures.
notes.loanToDepositRatio: Computed as gross loans (residential mortgages $277,246M + personal $46,388M + credit card $20,226M + business & government $210,047M = $553,907M, before allowance for credit losses) ÷ total deposits ($743,446M), per CIBC's unaudited consolidated balance sheet as at July 31, 2024.
notes.retailDepositsPct: Personal deposits ($250,231M) ÷ total deposits ($743,446M) per balance sheet Deposits note.
notes.wholesaleDepositsPct: Business and government ($414,178M) + Bank ($27,503M) + Secured borrowings ($51,534M) = $492,215M, ÷ total deposits $743,446M. 'Secured borrowings' (covered bond/securitization deposit notes) is treated as wholesale since it is not personal/retail.
notes.newMetricsSource: CIBC Report to Shareholders for the Third Quarter, 2024 (unaudited interim consolidated financial statements) — https://www.cibc.com/content/dam/cibc-public-assets/about-cibc/investor-relations/pdfs/quarterly-results/2024/q324report-en.pdf
notes.irrbbEveSensitivityPct: CIBC "Structural interest rate sensitivity – measures" table (Q3 2024 Report to Shareholders, disclosed quarterly). CIBC discloses only a +/-100bp parallel shock (2 of the 6 Basel scenarios). Most adverse: +100bp parallel increase gives EVE impact of -$1,325M (pre-tax, total CAD+USD) ÷ Tier 1 capital $48,751M (same report's capital table / Pillar 3 KM1) = -2.72%. Not equivalent to the worst of six Basel scenarios — CIBC shows only 2 of the 6 standard shocks. This %-of-Tier-1 framing is ours.
notes.irrbbNiiSensitivityPct: Same +/-100bp parallel-shock table. Worse of the two disclosed scenarios: -100bp parallel decrease gives projected 12-month NII impact of -$271M (pre-tax, total CAD+USD) ÷ Tier 1 capital $48,751M = -0.56%. A derived ratio for cross-bank comparability; CIBC does not itself express NII sensitivity as a percentage of any base.
notes.wholesaleFundingPct: CIBC's disclosed "wholesale funding sources" contractual-maturity table total of $200,394M at carrying value (Q3 2024 Report to Shareholders) ÷ total assets $1,021,407M = 19.62%. Excludes repo (CIBC's own table scope), matching CIBC's existing method. CIBC discloses this table every quarter.
notes.stableDepositsPct: Stable deposits $99,127M as a share of total retail and small-business deposits $216,240M ($99,127M stable + $117,113M less stable). Denominator is the retail and small-business book, so this bucket and less stable deposits sum to 100%.
notes.lessStableDepositsPct: Less stable deposits $117,113M as a share of total retail and small-business deposits $216,240M ($99,127M stable + $117,113M less stable). Denominator is the retail and small-business book, so this bucket and stable deposits sum to 100%.
notes.operationalDepositsPct: Operational deposits $110,273M as a share of total wholesale deposits $216,672M ($110,273M operational + $106,399M non-operational). Denominator is the wholesale book, so this bucket and non-operational deposits sum to 100%.
notes.nonOperationalDepositsPct: Non-operational deposits $106,399M as a share of total wholesale deposits $216,672M ($110,273M operational + $106,399M non-operational). Denominator is the wholesale book, so this bucket and operational deposits sum to 100%.
notes.tlacLeverageRatio: TLAC as a percentage of leverage ratio exposure, per OSFI's TLAC guideline. Cross-checked against an overlapping supplementary/Pillar 3 disclosure.
notes.dividendPayoutRatio: Reported basis, from CIBC's Supplementary Financial Information financial-highlights table.
notes.roa: Disclosed by the issuer: 0.71% return on average assets, read from the supplementary financial information (page 6), in the column headed Q3 2024. Not computed.
notes.adjustedOperatingLeverage: Disclosed: +0.6% adjusted operating leverage, read from the issuer's Q2 2026 financial supplementary information (page 6) in the column headed Q3 2024. Operating leverage is the difference between revenue growth and expense growth, so positive means revenue grew faster than costs.
notes.rotce: COMPUTED, not disclosed -- CIBC publishes no ROTCE. Net income attributable to common shareholders $1,823M, annualised over 92 days, divided by average tangible common equity $43,782M (average common equity $51,916M less goodwill and intangibles $8,134M) = 16.5%. All three operands are disclosed. Caveat: the goodwill/intangibles deduction is a period-end balance applied against an average equity base, because neither bank publishes an average deduction the way RBC does; goodwill moves slowly, so the effect is small but it is an approximation. Not directly comparable to the four banks that publish their own ROTCE.
notes.equityMultiplier: Computed from two disclosed figures: average total assets $1,012,012M divided by average common equity $51,916M = 19.49x. Both operands are published in the issuer's own financial supplementary information. Average COMMON equity is the denominator so the DuPont identity holds against the ROE and ROA already in this dataset (ROA x multiplier is approximately ROE).
notes.adjustedDilutedEps: Disclosed: $1.93 adjusted diluted earnings per share for Q3 2024. CIBC supplementary financial information p5, row "adjusted diluted EPS ($)". Adjusted measures remove each issuer's own items of note, so the adjustments differ between banks even though every figure here is the bank's own published number.

notes.irrbbNiiSensitivityPct: Same +/-100bp parallel shock table. Worse of the two scenarios: -100bp parallel decrease gives projected 12-month NII impact of -$242M (pre-tax, total). irrbbDisclosureNote: CIBC discloses interest rate risk in the banking book under the heading 'Structural interest rate sensitivity' in the MD&A of its Report to Shareholders every quarter (and again in the Annual Report at the Oct 31 fiscal year-end). It shows a single prescribed shock size (immediate and sustained +/-100 basis points, floored at zero), reporting both the projected 12-month pre-tax ΔNII and the pre-tax ΔEVE for each direction, split by CAD and USD. It does not publish the full Basel Committee six-scenario IRRBB1 standardized table (parallel up/down, steepener, flattener, short-rate up/down). This is industry-wide in Canada, not CIBC-specific: OSFI's Pillar 3 Disclosure Guideline for D-SIBs is only now (2026 consultation, comment period closed July 20, 2026) proposing to adopt the BCBS IRRBB1 template, with an expected effective date of fiscal Q4 2027 — so no current Canadian D-SIB publicly discloses the full six-scenario table yet. CIBC's disclosed sensitivities are not expressed as a percentage of any capital base by CIBC itself; the %-of-Tier-1 figures here are derived by dividing CIBC's disclosed dollar sensitivities by Tier 1 capital from the same report's capital table, for cross-bank comparability.
